title: Australian live bodies launch nationwide venue map for tour planning
summary: Australian live music industry organisations have launched a free-to-use national venue directory which aims to let agents and artists plan tours with its interactive tools. The service is known as the Australian Music Touring Network (AMTN) and launched with its website this week. title: Francophone music ‘a growing sensation’ after largest ever UK show
summary: After Congolese artist Fally Ipupa set a record for the largest Francophone concert in UK history, the artist’s representative says French-language music is “finally getting attention” internationally. After two consecutive nights at The O2 on 24 and 25 October, Rob Hallett, who represented Ipupa for the London dates, says the appetite for Congolese music has reached the point of supporting a run of European festival slots for Ipupa. “It’s a growing sensation. Francophone music is finally getting attention,” he tells IQ. title: District by Zomato strikes venue deal to support ‘next phase’ of India’s live evolution
summary: India’s District by Zomato has announced a “first-of-its-kind” strategic collaboration with telecommunications firm Airtel for the naming rights and investment in the digital infrastructure of one of the country’s only purpose-built venues. Under the agreement, the 17,000-capacity outdoor space in Bengaluru will be renamed from Terraform Arena to Airtel Arena, with the company investing in high-capacity digital infrastructure across the 16-acre site. The plug-and-play venue opened in November 2024, with District taking over operations last September. summary: South Korean entertainment giant HYBE has reported record quarterly revenue and operating profit, driven by its concert revenue almost tripling year-on-year in Q3. title: Luxembourg’s Rockhal grows outdoor series amid major venue ‘reimagining’
summary: Luxembourg’s Rockhal is gearing up for a year of transformation in 2027, with plans to expand its open-air concert series while undertaking a significant “reimagining” of its indoor venue, CEO Olivier Toth tells IQ. Open Air Belval will return in June next year, its fourth iteration since launching in 2018, with acts including Ireland’s Fontaines D.C., the UK’s Sting, Belgium’s Angèle, and Germany’s Die Fantastischen Vier already lined up to perform in the industrial setting outside the small arena.
